etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Adjective and determiner from Middle English scant, from Old Norse skamt, neuter of skammr (“short”), from Proto-Germanic *skammaz (“short”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱem- (“mutilated, hornless”). Verb from Middle English scanten, from the adjective. Noun and adverb from Middle English scant, from the adjective.
senses: Not full, large, or plentiful; scarcely sufficient; scanty; meager.
(transitive) To limit in amount or share; to stint.
(intransitive) To fail, or become less; to scantle.
(uncommon or dated) With difficulty; scarcely; hardly.
